Web searches (Sixtinus Coppenbruegge 1636 chiffrierte Korrespondenz; Sixtinus Calenberg Spion Chiffre; Deutsche Biographie entries for Wilhelm Burchard and Nicolaus Sixtinus) found biography only (jurist, Hessian and Schaumburg councillor, d. 1652 Hameln) and no edition or study of the seizure; the nearest cipher study, Waldispuehl/Kopal on a Kassel letter of 1637 to Oxenstierna, is a different correspondence. seen.cipher: German Kurrent letters in which names or words are replaced by graphic symbols inside the plain text: an open square, a square with a cross, an asterisk, a bar and cross, circles with a dot, double crosses and small numeral groups, on most lines of the left letter of image 020. No decipherment, interlinear gloss or key sheet is written on these leaves or filed beside them (images 15-27 inspected; the leaves are microfilm-style scans with a note that the original is faded).
